kitDescription: Noise is an Electric rocket-launcher Supporter whose entire kit is team survivability, not damage. When she is hit 20 times, all allies take reduced damage for 20 seconds. Each of her full-charge rockets taunts the enemy she hits for 2 seconds and grants her a brief 1.8-second Max HP boost. Her Burst I gives the whole team a heal-over-time — a percentage of her own final Max HP restored every second for 10 seconds — plus a 10-second Max HP increase scaled to each ally's own HP. On a damage-only board she contributes nothing beyond her bare rocket damage; her real value is mitigation, aggro control, and feeding teammates that react to recovery.

verdictRationale: No gotchas: all five kit lines are FAITHFUL (S2b self Max HP, burst heal cadence, burst team Max HP) or DOCUMENTED_GAP (S1 Damage Taken ▼, S2a taunt — both primitive-less and inert in the no-incoming-damage v1 sim, verbatim in `unmodeled` with ⚑ recipes). Convergence is strong where it matters: the S5 blind tests run GREEN against the driver's shipped override (9 passed; the 3 skips are the blind's own documented GAPs, not divergences), and the only S6 divergence — a zero-valued placeholder block mis-keying S1's trigger onto outgoing hits — resolves in the DRIVER's favor, since a clean documented UNMODELED is more faithful than a block that fires on an invented trigger. Discrimination holds on every load-bearing axis: S2b is proven self-scoped/per-shot/1.8s against the burst-keyed and long-window counterfactuals; the burst Max HP is proven target-scaled against the caster-scaled misread; the heal is proven ticks:10 against the ticks:1 collapse with crown's own self-heal stripped so the fixture isolates Noise as the sole recovery source; and the atkPct counterfactual proves the shipped Max-HP grants are the inert encodings, not smuggled damage buffs. Nothing must change for GO. Same-model residual for the owner to spot-check: the heal's first-tick phase (driver caveat claims an immediate first event then 9 more, ~9s span) is engine convention rather than footage-verified, and the 2.47% heal magnitude is unmodeled by design pending an HP pool — both documented, neither board-relevant under scope lock.
